plan.topic_summary: Quantum annealing is a quantum computing paradigm that exploits quantum tunneling to solve optimization and sampling problems. It matters for a 1–5 year view because it is the most commercially deployed quantum modality today, and whether it can demonstrate reproducible advantage over classical methods will shape the broader quantum computing market and investment thesis.
key_questions: What is the current state of demonstrated quantum advantage or parity for quantum annealing on commercially available hardware, and which problem classes show the strongest evidence?

How are qubit count, connectivity topology, and control electronics evolving, and what are the key physical bottlenecks (cryogenics, thermal noise, decoherence) limiting further scaling over the next 1–3 years?
What progress is being made on hybrid quantum-classical algorithms that combine annealing with classical post-processing to extend effective problem size beyond the native qubit count?

Can quantum annealing demonstrate a clear, reproducible advantage over the best classical solvers (including GPU and FPGA accelerators) on commercially relevant optimization problems within 3–5 years?

What is the competitive dynamic between quantum annealing and gate-based quantum computing for optimization workloads, and could gate-based approaches displace annealing as the dominant quantum modality for these problems?

What are the most credible near-term application domains (e.g., logistics, finance, materials discovery) where quantum annealing could generate measurable commercial value, and what is the expected timeline to revenue?

gaps: Error correction and error mitigation for quantum annealing is covered only at low confidence (R6) with limited settings; the path to practical fault-tolerant annealing remains under-evidenced.
Reproducibility of quantum annealing results across runs and hardware generations is not explicitly addressed in any finding, despite being a planned risk query.
Cryogenic engineering and control challenges (a planned science query) have no dedicated finding; the evidence on hardware engineering constraints is thin.

Several key findings (S5, S6, R5, R6, R7, R8) carry low confidence, meaning the report must hedge on multi-objective optimization gains, multi-tasking scalability, adiabatic scaling limits, and whether application gains are truly quantum.
Market evidence is dominated by D-Wave's own 10-K filings (M1–M5); independent third-party commercial validation is absent.

sources.title: On Quantum Annealing Without a Physical Quantum Annealer
sources.abstract: Quantum annealing is an emerging metaheuristic used for solving combinatorial optimisation problems. However, hardware based physical quantum annealers are primarily limited to a single vendor. As an alternative, we can discretise the quantum annealing process (discretised quantum annealing or DiQA) and use it on gate-model quantum computers. In this work, we first benchmark DiQA against simulated annealing for a similar number of steps. We then propose and evaluate a hybrid quantum classical heuristic: Quantum Accelerated Simulated Annealing (QASA), where the traditional classical annealing procedure can be sped up with the use of (relatively) low depth DiQA circuits. This is done by (i) running a partial annealing scheme with a fraction of the depth of the complete circuit (ii) sampling the results from the circuit and fitting a Gibbs distribution on it and (iii) Using the inverse temperature of the Gibbs distribution and the best sample to initialise simulated annealing (SA). Our simulation results show QASA performing comparably to SA but for a reduced amount of steps. With the promising results of our work, we hope to generate interest for potential future work in the area of fixed-parameter quantum optimisation.

sources.title: Toward Computing Bounds for Ramsey Numbers Using Quantum Annealing
sources.venue: Toward computing bounds for Ramsey numbers using quantum annealing. Quantum Inf Process 24, 221 (2025)
sources.abstract: Quantum annealing is a powerful tool for solving and approximating combinatorial optimization problems such as graph partitioning, community detection, centrality, routing problems, and more. In this paper we explore the use of quantum annealing as a tool for use in exploring combinatorial mathematics research problems. We consider the monochromatic triangle problem and the Ramsey number problem, both examples of graph coloring. Conversion to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form is required to run on quantum hardware. While the monochromatic triangle problem is quadratic by nature, the Ramsey number problem requires the use of order reduction methods for a quadratic formulation. We discuss implementations, limitations, and results when running on the D-Wave Advantage quantum annealer.

sources.title: Quantum Similarity-Driven QUBO Framework for Multi-Period Supply Chain Allocation using Time-Multiplexed Coherent Ising Machines and Simulated Quantum Annealing
sources.abstract: Multi-period stock-keeping unit (SKU) allocation in supply chains is a combinatorial optimization problem that is both NP-hard and operationally critical, requiring simultaneous attention to profitability, feasibility, and diversity. Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) provides a principled framework for such tasks, yet prior studies often rely on simplified assumptions or omit real operational constraints. This work proposes a hybrid QUBO framework integrating three advances: (i) a quantum-derived similarity kernel, obtained from a variational RX embedding, to discourage redundant SKU selections; (ii) exact per-period capacity enforcement via slack-bit encoding to maintain feasibility; and (iii) execution on a time-multiplexed Coherent Ising Machine (CIM) benchmarked against simulated quantum annealing (SQA) and classical optimization algorithms. The resulting model, with over one million quadratic terms and about 4,100 variables, captures profit, risk, and capacity interactions within a unified formulation. On a dataset of 500 SKUs across eight planning periods, Quanfluence's CIM achieved an energy of minus 2.95 times 10 to the power of 16, producing robust solutions with 288 distinct SKUs (approximately 60 percent of the catalog), 226,813 allocated units, and 12.75 million dollars profit, all with zero capacity violations. These results demonstrate that hybrid quantum-classical QUBO methods can deliver feasible and profitable supply-chain allocations at an industrial scale.

sources.title: Scaling Advantage in Approximate Optimization with Quantum Annealing
sources.abstract: Quantum annealing is a heuristic optimization algorithm that exploits quantum evolution to find low-energy states. Quantum annealers have scaled up in recent years to tackle increasingly larger and more highly connected discrete optimization and quantum simulation problems. Nevertheless, a computational quantum advantage in exact optimization using quantum annealing hardware has so far remained elusive. Here, we present evidence for a quantum annealing scaling advantage in approximate optimization. The advantage is relative to the top classical heuristic algorithm: parallel tempering with isoenergetic cluster moves (PT-ICM). The setting is a family of 2D spin-glass problems with high-precision spin-spin interactions. To achieve this advantage, we implement quantum annealing correction (QAC): an embedding of a bit-flip error-correcting code with energy penalties that leverages the properties of the D-Wave Advantage quantum annealer to yield over 1,300 error-suppressed logical qubits on a degree-5 interaction graph. We generate random spin-glass instances on this graph and benchmark their time-to-epsilon, a generalization of the time-to-solution metric for low-energy states. We demonstrate that, with QAC, quantum annealing exhibits a scaling advantage over PT-ICM at sampling low-energy states with an optimality gap of at least 1.0%. This amounts to the first demonstration of an algorithmic quantum speedup in approximate optimization.

sources.title: Comparison of D-Wave Quantum Annealing and Gibbs Monte Carlo for Sampling from a Probability Distribution of a Restricted Boltzmann Machine
sources.abstract: A local-valley (LV) centered approach to assessing the quality of sampling from Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) was applied to the latest generation of the D-Wave quantum annealer. D-Wave and Gibbs samples from a classically trained RBM were obtained at conditions relevant to the contrastive-divergence-based RBM learning. The samples were compared for the number of the LVs to which they belonged and the energy of the corresponding local minima. No significant (desirable) increase in the number of the LVs has been achieved by decreasing the D-Wave annealing time. At any training epoch, the states sampled by the D-Wave belonged to a somewhat higher number of LVs than in the Gibbs sampling. However, many of those LVs found by the two techniques differed. For high-probability sampled states, the two techniques were (unfavorably) less complementary and more overlapping. Nevertheless, many potentially "important" local minima, i.e., those having intermediate, even if not high, probability values, were found by only one of the two sampling techniques while missed by the other. The two techniques overlapped less at later than earlier training epochs, which is precisely the stage of the training when modest improvements to the sampling quality could make meaningful differences for the RBM trainability. The results of this work may explain the failure of previous investigations to achieve substantial (or any) improvement when using D-Wave-based sampling. However, the results reveal some potential for improvement, e.g., using a combined classical-quantum approach.

sources.title: Quantum Annealing
sources.abstract: Abstract Quantum annealing is a quantum optimization approach designed to solve complex problems that require finding the optimal solution among a vast number of choices. These problems are often difficult or impossible for classical computers to handle efficiently. This chapter examines the role of quantum annealing in addressing such challenges, showcasing its potential through existing applications and discussing the opportunities and limitations of these systems. It also presents a strategic roadmap for applying quantum annealing technologies in the defense sector, highlighting their importance and potential for solving intricate optimization tasks.

sources.title: Quantum Topology Optimization via Quantum Annealing
sources.abstract: We present a quantum annealing-based solution method for topology optimization (TO). In particular, we consider TO in a more general setting, i.e., applied to structures of continuum domains where designs are represented as distributed functions, referred to as continuum TO problems. According to the problem's properties and structure, we formulate appropriate sub-problems that can be solved on an annealing-based quantum computer. The methodology established can effectively tackle continuum TO problems formulated as mixed-integer nonlinear programs. To maintain the resulting sub-problems small enough to be solved on quantum computers currently accessible with small numbers of qubits and limited connectivity, we further develop a splitting approach that splits the problem into two parts: the first part can be efficiently solved on classical computers, and the second part with a reduced number of variables is solved on a quantum computer. By such, a practical continuum TO problem of varying scales can be handled on the D-Wave quantum annealer. More specifically, we concern the minimum compliance, a canonical TO problem that seeks an optimal distribution of materials to minimize the compliance with desired material usage. The superior performance of the developed methodology is assessed and compared with the stateof-the-art heuristic classical methods, in terms of both solution quality and computational efficiency. The present work hence provides a promising new avenue of applying quantum computing to practical designs of topology for various applications.

sources.title: Multi-objective optimization by quantum annealing
sources.abstract: An important task in multi-objective optimization is generating the Pareto front -- the set of all Pareto-optimal compromises among multiple objective functions applied to the same set of variables. Since this task can be computationally intensive even for small problems, it is a natural target for quantum optimization. Indeed, this problem was recently approached using the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) on an IBM gate-model processor. Here we compare these QAOA results with quantum annealing on the same two input problems, using the same methodology. We find that quantum annealing vastly outperforms not just QAOA run on the IBM processor, but all classical and quantum methods analyzed in the previous study. On the harder problem, quantum annealing improves upon the best known Pareto front. This small study reinforces the promise of quantum annealing in multi-objective optimization.

sources.title: On the emerging potential of quantum annealing hardware for combinatorial optimization
sources.abstract: Abstract Over the past decade, the usefulness of quantum annealing hardware for combinatorial optimization has been the subject of much debate. Thus far, experimental benchmarking studies have indicated that quantum annealing hardware does not provide an irrefutable performance gain over state-of-the-art optimization methods. However, as this hardware continues to evolve, each new iteration brings improved performance and warrants further benchmarking. To that end, this work conducts an optimization performance assessment of D-Wave Systems’ Advantage Performance Update computer, which can natively solve sparse unconstrained quadratic optimization problems with over 5,000 binary decision variables and 40,000 quadratic terms. We demonstrate that classes of contrived problems exist where this quantum annealer can provide run time benefits over a collection of established classical solution methods that represent the current state-of-the-art for benchmarking quantum annealing hardware. Although this work does not present strong evidence of an irrefutable performance benefit for this emerging optimization technology, it does exhibit encouraging progress, signaling the potential impacts on practical optimization tasks in the future.

sources.title: Multi-tasking through quantum annealing
sources.abstract: Quantum annealing approximately solves combinatorial optimization problems by leveraging the principles of adiabatic quantum systems. In this approach, the system's Hamiltonian evolves from an initial general state to a problem-specific state. This study introduces multi-tasking quantum annealing (MTQA), a method that enables the parallel processing of multiple optimization problems by embedding them into spatially distinct regions on quantum hardware. MTQA is evaluated using two NP-hard problems: the minimum vertex cover problem (MVCP) and the graph partitioning problem (GPP). This parallel approach optimizes quantum resource utilization by concurrently utilizing idle qubits. The findings demonstrate that MTQA achieves a solution quality comparable to single-problem quantum annealing and classical simulated annealing (SA), while notably reducing the time-to-solution (TTS) metrics. Eigenspectrum analysis further theoretically supports the hypothesis that parallel embedding preserves quantum coherence and does not increase computational complexity by efficiently utilizing available quantum hardware (e.g., qubits and couplers). MTQA enables efficient multitasking in quantum annealing, optimizing hardware utilization and improving throughput for concurrent tasks and demonstrating performance for problems up to 100 nodes in real-world applications.

sources.title: Can Constrained Quantum Annealing Be Effective in Noisy Quantum Annealers?
sources.abstract: We investigate the performance of penalty-based quantum annealing (PQA) and constrained quantum annealing (CQA) in solving the graph partitioning problem under various noise models, including depolarizing, bit-flip, and phase-flip noise. We found that even in the absence of noise, the relative superiority of PQA or CQA is highly problem-dependent. PQA generally demonstrates relatively stable success probabilities, while CQA's performance varies significantly across problem instances. Notably, CQA experiences leakage from the constraint-satisfying subspace under most noise models, with the exception of phase-flip noise, where no leakage occurs exactly. The dependence of success probability on noise strength reveals that PQA consistently outperforms CQA in the weak noise regime, whereas CQA achieves higher success probabilities under strong phase-flip noise. However, even in this case, the overall success probability remains low, suggesting that CQA is not yet practical for noisy quantum annealers without the development of error-corrected quantum annealing and autonomous error correction techniques to address leakage from the constraint-satisfying subspace. To confine the system within the constraint subspace in CQA, error correction methods and cat code encoding will likely be required, both of which can suppress bit-flip errors.

sources.title: Quantum annealing and condensed matter physics
sources.abstract: Quantum annealing leverages the properties of interacting quantum spin systems to solve computational problems, typically optimisation problems. Current hardware now has capabilities that can be used to solve condensed matter physics problems, too. In this topical review, we provide an overview of quantum annealing aimed at condensed matter physicists, to show the mutual benefits of working together to understand and improve how quantum annealers work, and to use them to advance condensed matter physics.

Constrained quantum annealing leaks from the constraint-satisfying subspace under most noise models and remains impractical on noisy annealers without error correction.

limitations: All findings are based on titles and abstracts only; no full texts were read.
The sample is small (12 items) and heterogeneous, mixing preprints, journal articles, a book chapter and a review, so cross-paper comparison is indicative rather than systematic.

sources.title: Quantum error mitigation in quantum annealing
sources.abstract: Abstract Quantum error mitigation (QEM) presents a promising near-term approach to reducing errors when estimating expectation values in quantum computing. Here, we introduce QEM techniques tailored for quantum annealing, using zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE). We implement ZNE through zero-temperature and zero-time extrapolations. The practical zero-time extrapolation developed exploits the Kibble-Zurek mechanism so that only problem-Hamiltonian rescaling is required. We conduct experimental investigations into the quantum critical and post-critical dynamics of a transverse-field Ising spin chain by examining statistics with weak and strong post-critical dynamics. We demonstrate successful mitigation of thermal noise and non-thermal errors through both of these extrapolation techniques.

sources.title: Superpixel-Based QUBO for Scalable Quantum-Enhanced Medical Image Segmentation
sources.abstract: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) has emerged as a powerful framework for medical computing problems. Binary decision variables naturally represent clinical choices, making QUBO formulations well-suited for quantum annealing hardware. However, a fundamental scalability challenge limits practical deployment: problem size grows rapidly with input dimensionality, creating computational bottlenecks that restrict applications to simplified scenarios. This paper addresses this challenge through hierarchical problem reduction, as demonstrated in medical image segmentation, where pixel-level QUBO formulations create over 65,000 variables for a 256x256 image, forcing existing approaches to downsample to 42x42 resolution and discard 97% of pixel information. A superpixel-based QUBO framework is proposed using simple linear iterative clustering (SLIC) to group pixels into perceptually meaningful regions, then formulate segmentation as QUBO over a region adjacency graph (RAG) combining min-cut and smoothness objectives. Validation on INbreast mammography breast cancer images demonstrates a 4.2% improvement in segmentation quality (mean IoU 0.76 vs 0.73) with 33 computational speedup (0.67s vs 21.97s) and a 97.3% reduction in problem size (1764 to 48 variables), all achieved while processing full-resolution images rather than downsampled versions. The reduced problem size also fits well within current quantum annealer connectivity limits, removing the embedding overhead that has historically blocked direct deployment of pixel-level QUBO segmentation on quantum hardware.

sources.title: Signatures of Open and Noisy Quantum Systems in Single-Qubit Quantum Annealing
sources.abstract: We propose a quantum annealing protocol that effectively probes the dynamics of a single qubit on D-Wave's quantum annealing hardware. This protocol uses D-Wave's $h$-gain schedule functionality, which allows the rapid suppression of the longitudinal magnetic field at arbitrary points during the anneal. This feature enables us to distinguish between open and closed-system dynamics as well as the presence and absence of longitudinal magnetic field noise. We show that thermal fluctuations alone are not sufficient to explain the system's dynamics and that a prominent role is played by magnetic field fluctuations, which need to be included in an open quantum system description. Moreover, our protocol only requires single-qubit measurements, which makes it suitable as an exploration and calibration tool for large-scale quantum annealing hardware.

sources.title: Effectiveness of quantum annealing for continuous-variable optimization
sources.abstract: The application of quantum annealing to the optimization of continuous-variable functions is a relatively unexplored area of research. We test the performance of quantum annealing applied to a one-dimensional continuous-variable function with a rugged energy landscape. After domain-wall encoding to map a continuous variable to discrete Ising variables, we first benchmark the performance of the real hardware, the D-Wave 2000Q, against several state-of-the-art classical optimization algorithms designed for continuous-variable problems to find that the D-Wave 2000Q matches the classical algorithms in a limited domain of computation time. Beyond this domain, classical global optimization algorithms outperform the quantum device. Next we examine several optimization algorithms that are applicable to the Ising formulation of the problem, such as the time-evolving block decimation (TEBD) to simulate ideal coherent quantum annealing, simulated annealing, simulated quantum annealing, and spin-vector Monte Carlo. The data show that TEBD's coherent quantum annealing achieves far better results than the other approaches, demonstrating the effectiveness of coherent tunneling. From these two types of benchmarks, we conclude that the hardware realization of quantum annealing has the potential to significantly outperform the best classical algorithms if thermal noise and other imperfections are sufficiently suppressed and the device operates coherently, as demonstrated in recent short-time quantum simulations.

sources.title: Embedding-aware noise modeling of quantum annealing
sources.abstract: Quantum annealing provides a practical realization of adiabatic quantum computation and has emerged as a promising approach for solving large-scale combinatorial optimization problems. However, current devices remain constrained by sparse hardware connectivity, which requires embedding logical variables into chains of physical qubits. This embedding overhead limits scalability and reduces reliability as longer chains are more prone to noise-induced errors. In this work, we develop an embedding-aware baseline noise framework that connects chain-length growth to accumulated integrated-control-error variance, chain break probability (CBP), chain break fraction (CBF), and chain-strength scaling. We distinguish a moment-level uncorrelated ICE baseline, which yields a linear variance law, from a Gaussian closure that gives a closed-form erfc approximation for CBP. Experiments on the D-Wave Advantage2 Zephyr processor show that the calibrated baseline model captures the dominant growth trend of CBF with embedding size. However, the empirical critical chain-strength exponent ranges from $$\alpha =0.805$$ to $$\alpha =1.006$$ across chain-break tolerance thresholds, with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals consistently excluding the independent-noise prediction $$\alpha =0.5$$ ; a direct fit of a correlated-variance extension recovers $$\gamma \approx 1.8$$ , consistent with the asymptotic relation $$\gamma =2\alpha $$ . These results indicate that real-hardware variance accumulation deviates from the independent-noise reference and is consistent with a correlated component. The proposed framework offers quantitative guidance for embedding-aware chain-strength tuning and motivates more general noise models incorporating correlated and non-Gaussian hardware effects.

sources.title: Finite-temperature criticality through quantum annealing
sources.abstract: Critical phenomena at finite temperature underpin a broad range of physical systems, yet their study remains challenging due to computational bottlenecks near phase transitions. Quantum annealers have attracted significant interest as a potential tool for accessing finite temperature criticality beyond classical reach, but their utility in precisely resolving criticality has remained limited by noise, hardware constraints, and thermal fluctuations. Here we overcome these challenges, introducing a sampling protocol that combines real-time temperature inference with fine control of the energy scales throughout experiments. A careful embedding strategy allows us to fully capture the finite-temperature critical behavior of the paradigmatic two-dimensional Ising ferromagnet on toroidal lattices up to 2640 spins. By tuning the energy scale of the system and mitigating device defects, we sample effective Boltzmann distributions extracting both the critical temperature and the associated universal critical exponents. Our approach opens the study of equilibrium and non-equilibrium critical phenomena in a broad class of systems at finite temperature.

sources.title: Thermal lifetime of the centralized repetition code: From quantum annealing to social dynamics
sources.abstract: There is an extensive body of research probing the potential of adiabatic quantum computation and quantum annealing to solve hard computational problems. This research endeavor is complicated by noise afflicting hardware during the computational process. An error-correcting approach called quantum annealing correction (QAC) was suggested to mitigate this noise. The QAC approach employs a centralized version of the repetition code in which the qubits are configured in a star-graph pattern with one special qubit playing the role of the hub. In this paper, we explore the thermal physics of the centralized repetition code, using a Lindblad equation framework to analyze its lifetime when coupled to a thermal bath. We show that its centralized configuration leads to thermal stability, enabling the robust storage of a logical bit of information, despite the fact that there is only 1 ferromagnetic Ising interaction per qubit like a 1-dimensional Ising chain.

sources.title: Statistical Qubit Freezing Extending Physical Limit of Quantum Annealers
sources.abstract: Adiabatic quantum annealers encounter scalability challenges due to exponentially fast diminishing energy gaps between ground and excited states with qubit-count increase. This introduces errors in identifying ground states compounded by a thermal noise. We propose a novel algorithmic scheme called statistical qubit freezing (SQF) that selectively fixes the state of statistically deterministic qubit in the annealing Hamiltonian model of the given problem. Applying freezing repeatedly, SQF significantly enhances the spectral gap between of an adiabatic process, as an example, by up to 60\% compared to traditional annealing methods in the standard D-Wave's quantum Ising machine solution, effectively overcoming the fundamental limitations.

sources.title: Using domain walls to benchmark fast quantum anneals
sources.abstract: We consider the distribution of domain walls arising in ground states of frustrated 1-dimensional Ising spin chains with anti-parallel boundary spins. For ideal chains, a sine-squared particle-in-a-box distribution of domain walls is expected in the quantum setting, and a uniform distribution expected classically. However, for chains with random imperfections, prior work [Chancellor et al., npj Quantum Inf. 8, 73, 2022] found that the distribution in a physical implementation corresponded to neither. Instead, the domain wall distribution forms a U-shaped profile arising from a classical model with random fields, where the combination of averaging over these fields and thermal averaging produces the characteristic U-shape. With D-Wave's newer fast anneal feature, we access anneal times shorter than the coherence time and observe the expected coherent quantum behavior in the form of a sine-squared distribution. For the shortest available anneal time, the dynamics have not yet reached the sine-squared shape and instead display a different U-shape in the middle of the chains. This motivates using the extent of the domain wall distribution tail in this regime as a platform independent metric that provides a signature of both coherence time and noise levels.

sources.title: Quantum annealers as programmable thermal machines
sources.abstract: Programmable quantum annealers are used for optimization, probabilistic sampling, and simulation, but their performance is commonly reported without the energy exchanged during computation. Here we characterize the D-Wave quantum annealer as a closed thermodynamic cycle. From initial and final Ising energies and an effective temperature fitted to the output distribution, we obtain lower bounds on entropy production, environment energy exchange, work, and power. By varying the prepared distribution and the reverse annealing turning point, we map heater-, accelerator-, refrigerator-, and engine-compatible regimes in one dimensional chains and higher connectivity instances, and apply the same analysis to Advantage and Advantage2 hardware. For an encoded optimization problem, the measured processor energy change states whether final candidates improve or worsen the programmed objective on average. For sampling, the fitted temperature provides an operational measure of how strongly probability is concentrated among low energy configurations. The thermodynamic mode therefore adds information absent from solution quality or runtime alone: it distinguishes driven refinement, net heating, and heat pumping while quantifying their energetic consequences. This framework connects quantum optimization, probabilistic computing, statistical physics simulation, hardware diagnostics, and energy-aware assessment without assuming that a thermodynamic label alone determines computational performance.

sources.title: Quantum annealing for combinatorial optimization: a benchmarking study
sources.abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) has the potential to significantly improve solution quality and reduce time complexity in solving combinatorial optimization problems compared to classical optimization methods. However, due to the limited number of qubits and their connectivity, the QA hardware did not show such an advantage over classical methods in past benchmarking studies. Recent advancements in QA with more than 5000 qubits, enhanced qubit connectivity, and the hybrid architecture promise to realize the quantum advantage. Here, we use a quantum annealer with state-of-the-art techniques and benchmark its performance against classical solvers. To compare their performance, we solve over 50 optimization problem instances represented by large and dense Hamiltonian matrices using quantum and classical solvers. The results demonstrate that a state-of-the-art quantum solver has higher accuracy (~0.013%) and a significantly faster problem-solving time (~6561×) than the best classical solver. Our results highlight the advantages of leveraging QA over classical counterparts, particularly in hybrid configurations, for achieving high accuracy and substantially reduced problem solving time in large-scale real-world optimization problems.

findings.claim: Sparse qubit connectivity forces logical variables into chains of physical qubits. Longer chains are more error-prone, and real-hardware noise accumulates faster than the independent-noise baseline predicts, so the embedding overhead is a reliability limit on problem size.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The abstract reports fitted chain-strength exponents of about 0.8 to 1.0 whose confidence intervals exclude the independent-noise value of 0.5. That points to correlated noise. This is one study on one processor family, and the abstract is truncated before its conclusion.
findings.supporting_excerpt: This embedding overhead limits scalability and reduces reliability as longer chains are more prone to noise-induced errors.

findings.claim: On a continuous-variable benchmark, a D-Wave 2000Q matched classical optimizers only within a limited computation-time window, and classical global optimizers did better outside it. The authors' argument for a quantum edge depends on coherence being restored and on noise being suppressed, which is not yet shown on the hardware.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The test is a one-dimensional function on an older device generation. The 'potential to significantly outperform' conclusion rests on TEBD, a simulation of ideal coherent annealing, not on hardware results. Simulation-only evidence should not be read as a hardware capability.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Beyond this domain, classical global optimization algorithms outperform the quantum device.

findings.claim: Benchmark evidence on advantage is inconsistent. One study reports ~6561x faster solving and ~0.013% higher accuracy than the best classical solver. Its own introduction concedes that past studies showed no advantage, and the continuous-variable study found classical methods ahead outside a narrow window.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The abstract of src_c6db09ce69 credits the gain to 'a state-of-the-art quantum solver' and stresses hybrid configurations, so the quantum contribution is hard to separate from classical components. It does not say which classical solvers were used, how they were tuned, or how time was measured. A 0.013% accuracy gain is small. The result comes from one group on one problem family (large, dense Hamiltonians) and needs independent replication. Whether the speed comparison is like-for-like cannot be assessed from the abstract.
findings.supporting_excerpt: However, due to the limited number of qubits and their connectivity, the QA hardware did not show such an advantage over classical methods in past benchmarking studies.

findings.claim: Open-system noise is a first-order problem for current annealers. Thermal fluctuations alone do not explain single-qubit dynamics, and longitudinal magnetic-field noise matters. Coherent behavior is seen only in fast anneals shorter than the coherence time, while slower anneals on imperfect chains gave a classical-like signature.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_351899c14d (peer reviewed) shows non-thermal field noise. src_636e6b621d (arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed) reports that the expected coherent distribution appears only with the fast-anneal feature. Together they suggest standard-length anneals are noise-dominated. Both use simple 1D or single-qubit test cases, and the abstracts do not show how this carries over to large optimization problems.
findings.supporting_excerpt: We show that thermal fluctuations alone are not sufficient to explain the system's dynamics and that a prominent role is played by magnetic field fluctuations

findings.claim: The adiabatic scaling limit is not resolved. Energy gaps are reported to shrink exponentially with qubit count, and the proposed workaround (statistical qubit freezing) is shown only as a spectral-gap improvement of up to 60%, not as better solutions on a hard benchmark.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: This is an arXiv preprint with 2 citations. A 60% gap increase does not offset an exponential closing of the gap, and the abstract does not report time-to-solution. Its wording that the method is 'effectively overcoming the fundamental limitations' goes beyond what the abstract shows. Fixing qubits that are 'statistically deterministic' may also depend on prior knowledge of the answer, which the abstract does not address.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Adiabatic quantum annealers encounter scalability challenges due to exponentially fast diminishing energy gaps between ground and excited states with qubit-count increase.

findings.claim: Error mitigation and error correction for annealing are shown only in limited settings: ZNE on a transverse-field Ising spin chain, and a theoretical Lindblad analysis of the centralized repetition code used in quantum annealing correction. Neither shows that they improve the solution quality of general optimization problems at scale.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_3ad05e4ddc is peer reviewed but targets expectation values in a physics model system. src_d20e3989fd is an arXiv preprint and theoretical. The absence of demonstrations on practical optimization is a gap in the evidence retrieved here, not proof of failure. Overheads such as extra qubits and runs are not described in the abstracts.

findings.claim: The application papers rely on classical preprocessing or decomposition to fit problems onto the annealer, so their gains may come from problem reduction and not from quantum speedup. Examples are superpixel reduction from 1764 to 48 variables and a topology-optimization method that solves one part classically.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_32c1420450 is an arXiv preprint tested on one dataset (INbreast). It reports a 33x speedup and a 4.2% IoU gain, but the abstract does not say whether a purely classical solver on the same reduced problem would do as well. The pixel-level QUBO grows to over 65,000 variables, which shows the raw scaling barrier. src_4a335fbc67 compares to 'state-of-the-art heuristic classical methods', but the abstract excerpt does not name them or give figures, and the 'superior performance' claim cannot be checked from it.

findings.claim: Demonstrations of 'beyond classical' physics use on annealers still need heavy calibration (temperature inference, energy-scale tuning, defect mitigation, careful embedding). The showcased system is a 2D Ising ferromagnet on up to 2640 spins, which is a well-understood model.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The abstract of src_55f484ebaa says noise, hardware constraints and thermal fluctuations have limited use, and that they are overcome here by protocol design. That success is shown on a benchmark where classical methods are also well established (my background knowledge, not from the abstracts). The abstract does not claim a classical-intractable result. Separately, src_9f4f04f202 (arXiv preprint) says energy exchange is commonly not reported with performance, so energy cost is an unquantified gap, not a demonstrated problem.

hype_flags: '~6561x faster' and 'higher accuracy' than the best classical solver: from a hybrid solver, with unclear classical baselines and a tiny accuracy gain; it conflicts with other benchmark evidence
'Quantum advantage' and 'promise to realize the quantum advantage': wording about promise, not demonstrated advantage
'Effectively overcoming the fundamental limitations' (qubit freezing): a spectral-gap change, not shown scaling or solution-quality gains
'Quantum-enhanced' and 'quantum speedup' for applications (medical imaging, topology optimization): gains may come from classical problem reduction
'Beyond classical reach' for finite-temperature criticality: stated as a potential, and demonstrated on a standard Ising model
'Superior performance' versus classical heuristics (topology optimization): no numbers visible in the abstract

finding.claim: S1 presents the PRL scaling-advantage result without its qualifiers. The abstract limits the advantage to approximate optimization (optimality gap of at least 1.0%) on one constructed family of random 2D spin-glass instances with high-precision couplings. These instances sit on a degree-5 graph native to the hardware and were benchmarked against a single classical heuristic, PT-ICM. The finding gives no weight to these limits, nor to the fact that the authors themselves say exact-optimization advantage 'has so far remained elusive'. The evidence is also a single experimental group's result, and no independent replication is available in the evidence set.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstract itself restricts the claim to approximate optimization on a specific spin-glass family. 'First demonstration' is the authors' own framing and should be attributed as such, not repeated as established fact. Whether the advantage generalizes to other problem structures or other classical solvers is not shown in the abstract.
finding.supporting_excerpt: a computational quantum advantage in exact optimization using quantum annealing hardware has so far remained elusive. Here, we present evidence for a quantum annealing scaling advantage in approximate optimization.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S1–S3 omit the inconsistent benchmark evidence. One study (src_c6db09ce69) reports ~6561x faster solving and ~0.013% higher accuracy than the best classical solver, using hybrid configurations. Another (src_3305664d62) finds classical optimizers ahead outside a narrow computation-time window. The synthesis in S3 says generalized superiority 'remains unsupported' but does not mention that the evidence base is split. It also does not mention that 'quantum solver' results may reflect hybrid classical components, so they are not clean evidence of quantum speedup.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Strong speedup claims and negative results both exist in the retrieved abstracts. S3 should state that the field is contested and that headline speedups depend on which classical baseline and which solver configuration (hybrid or pure QPU) is used. Only abstracts were available, so the baseline details cannot be checked here.

finding.claim: S3 draws a stronger general conclusion than the cited papers allow. Two of its four citations (src_8f760685b0 on constrained annealing under noise, and src_2636467255 on RBM sampling) do not test whether annealing beats classical heuristics on problem families. One is a noise-model study of graph partitioning, and the other compares sampling overlap. Using them as support for 'narrow and conditional advantages' is a stretch. S3 also leaves out the hardware-level obstacles that explain why advantages are narrow: embedding chain errors, open-system noise and the exponentially shrinking gaps.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The cited sources are mixed in kind. src_8f760685b0 and src_2636467255 address noise and sampling quality, not advantage claims. The risk papers src_5794666bc4 and src_351899c14d show noise accumulating beyond independent-noise predictions and open-system effects playing a prominent role, so noise could be the stated cause. The stated conclusion is plausible but weakly grounded in the citations given.

finding.claim: S4 is a simulation-style noise study of graph partitioning that is a preprint with no peer-review signal in the evidence. It presents results from simulated noise models (depolarizing, bit-flip, phase-flip) as findings about 'noisy annealers'. The abstract says the relative superiority of penalty-based and constrained annealing is 'highly problem-dependent' even without noise. S4 omits this and the finding that penalty-based annealing outperforms in the weak-noise regime. The 'not yet practical' verdict is also the authors' judgment, not a measured hardware result.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstract describes noise-model analysis, not experiments on a physical D-Wave device. The conclusion about practicality on real annealers is therefore an extrapolation from idealized noise models.
finding.supporting_excerpt: We found that even in the absence of noise, the relative superiority of PQA or CQA is highly problem-dependent.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S5 and S6 overstate preliminary preprint results. In S5, the abstract says 'vastly outperforms' on only two input problems, and the authors call it a 'small study'. The comparison inherits the earlier QAOA study's methodology and does not test against modern classical solvers. S5 itself carries 'low' severity but is labelled verified_fact without noting the narrow basis. In S6, the abstract's 'comparable' quality and shorter time-to-solution are for problems up to 100 nodes, which are small enough for classical solvers to handle trivially. The 'preserves quantum coherence' point rests on a theoretical eigenspectrum analysis. Neither result shows advantage at useful scale.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The authors' own 'small study' wording limits the generality of S5. For S6, time-to-solution gains come from parallel packing of problems, which is a throughput effect and not a solution-quality or scaling advantage.
finding.supporting_excerpt: This small study reinforces the promise of quantum annealing in multi-objective optimization.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S8 and S9 present application results without isolating a quantum contribution. In S8, the method solves part of the problem classically and sends a reduced subproblem to the annealer; the abstract's 'superior performance' claim says nothing about how much of the gain comes from the annealer. In S9, the supply-chain result is a Coherent Ising Machine, which is not a quantum annealer, and the abstract reports zero capacity violations and a profit figure but no head-to-head solution-quality advantage over classical optimizers. 'Zero violations' follows from exact slack-bit encoding and is not evidence of quantum benefit. The DiQA/QASA result is from simulation only.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstracts show classical decomposition and reduction (src_4a335fbc67; src_32c1420450 reduces 1764 variables to 48). The QASA finding is simulation-only. Including CIM results under the topic 'quantum annealing' risks conflating different hardware. The reported figures cannot be read as evidence of quantum advantage.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Our simulation results show QASA performing comparably to SA but for a reduced amount of steps.

finding.claim: The findings ignore hardware reliability and scaling limits that bear on whether any demonstrated advantage can extend. These include chain-embedding overhead (error rates grow faster with chain length than independent-noise models predict), open-system noise, and exponentially shrinking energy gaps. Error correction and mitigation for annealing have only been shown in limited settings (a spin chain, and a theoretical Lindblad analysis). S1's QAC result is the main exception, and it is not discussed together with these limits.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Embedding overhead and noise are directly stated in the abstract and bear on problem size and reliability. The additional context (limited mitigation demonstrations, unresolved gap scaling) is my interpretation of the other abstracts.
finding.supporting_excerpt: This embedding overhead limits scalability and reduces reliability as longer chains are more prone to noise-induced errors.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S10 reads breadth of application exploration as meaningful progress, but the cited items give little evidence of effectiveness. The Ramsey-number paper discusses 'implementations, limitations, and results' without any reported advantage. The defense-sector chapter is a roadmap/overview. The condensed-matter paper is a topical review. 'Broadening use-case exploration' says nothing about whether annealing helps in these areas, and the physics-simulation uses need heavy calibration for a well-understood 2D Ising model.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: These are exploratory, review or roadmap documents. The finding is carefully low-severity, but it could imply more maturity than the abstracts show. The 'beyond classical' framing in src_55f484ebaa is a 'potential tool' claim and is applied to a well-understood model.
finding.supporting_excerpt: We discuss implementations, limitations, and results when running on the D-Wave Advantage quantum annealer.

limitations: Only 12 papers, abstracts only (some truncated); no methods, baselines or statistics could be checked.
Several key items are arXiv preprints (not peer reviewed): src_32c1420450, src_702ce7a0ed, src_d20e3989fd, src_636e6b621d, src_9f4f04f202.

The set is heavily D-Wave centered, with little on other annealing technologies (coherent Ising machines, digital annealers) or on classical alternatives such as GPU solvers, so displacement risk is under-covered.
No papers on cost, manufacturing, yield, cryogenics, power or supply concentration, so those risks are gaps in coverage, not findings.
Benchmark papers (src_c6db09ce69, src_3305664d62) use different problem types and hardware generations, so they cannot be directly reconciled.
Some metadata (e.g. 2026 publication dates) is taken as given; the sample is small and not systematic.
Only titles and abstracts were reviewed; details such as baselines, instance sizes and statistics in the full papers could change these judgments.

Many cited sources are preprints with no peer-review signal and zero or unknown citation counts, and the evidence set is small (23 papers), so absence of contradicting studies is not evidence of absence.
I did not search for independent replications or critiques of the QAC scaling-advantage result beyond the retrieved set, so S1 may be better or worse supported than shown here.
Several risk items rely on ai_interpretation because the abstracts do not state the problem directly.

sources.title: CYBER-PHYSICAL ARCHITECTURE FOR QUANTUM-ACCELERATED INDUSTRIAL MANUFACTURING AND AUTONOMOUS EXPERIMENTATION [US20260339300A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A hybrid quantum-classical cyber-physical control architecture for real-time optimization and automated actuation of complex industrial processes, including an industrial digestive system configured to transform heterogeneous feedstocks into valuable resources. The system continuously ingests streaming analog telemetry from physical sensor networks, utilizing a quantum industrial problem compiler to dynamically convert process states and multi-objective physical constraints into structurally bounded, quantum-computable representations. A latency-aware orchestrator dispatches these artifacts to quantum computing resources while managing deterministic classical fallbacks to ensure continuous operation. To safely bridge quantum optimization insights with rigid physical hardware limits, an actuation stability gateway decodes quantum candidate solutions, applies reverse-scaling, and utilizes mathematical gradient dampening on out-of-bounds parameters prior to mechanical actuation. The architecture further enables multi-site graph partitioning and an automated high-throughput experimentation discovery loop, providing continuous, self-learning adaptation and optimized resource recovery across dynamic manufacturing environments.

sources.title: Quantum Annealer-based Combinatorial Optimization Consulting System [KR20260144716A]
Method and System for Solving Optimization Problems [LU509917B1]
sources.abstract: The present invention relates to a computer-implemented method 100 and system for solving optimization problems using a quantum processing unit with multiple qubits and quantum gates. The method employs a tree-based optimization approach, for example a branch-and-bound or cut technique, integrated with a bias-field digitized counter-diabatic quantum optimization algorithm. It involves encoding the optimization problem into a problem Hamiltonian, initializing a time- dependent Hamiltonian, and applying a bias field. The quantum processing unit evolves the quantum state to reach the ground state of the problem Hamiltonian, followed by measuring and computing expectation values. The present invention constructs a tree of branches based on selected qubits, applying constraints to explore configurations that yield the lowest expectation values. Ultimately, it determines the optimal solution by extracting a bitstring from the final probability distribution, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of solving complex optimization problems.

sources.title: Quantum-Enhanced Gen-AI Approach for Optimizing Model Accuracy and Privacy in Secure Collaborative Analytics [US20260280861A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A system and method for secure collaborative analytics enable multiple parties to perform joint data analysis without exposing sensitive information. The invention integrates quantum computing, advanced cryptographic protocols, and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to ensure privacy, accuracy, and efficiency. Private datasets undergo quantum optimization to retain significant features, followed by encryption using quantum-resistant protocols. Encrypted data is securely transmitted and analyzed collaboratively using quantum homomorphic encryption, allowing computations directly on encrypted datasets. GenAI optimizes feature selection, computation workflows, and privacy-accuracy trade-offs, enabling iterative refinement of analytical outputs. Results are decrypted securely using quantum key authentication and validated against predefined benchmarks. The system employs differential privacy to protect individual records while preserving data utility and supports a blockchain-like ledger for immutable audit trails. Scalable, adaptable, and compatible with diverse data types, this invention addresses the evolving demands of secure, efficient, and collaborative analytics across various domains.

sources.title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS TO PERFORM INSTANTANEOUS QUBIT STATE READOUT IN A QUANTUM PROCESSOR [WO2026187636A2]
sources.abstract: Mid-anneal readout of qubits during can be used to characterize quantum processor dynamics. A method can comprise: initiating a state change of qubits; performing fast quantum annealing of detector rf-SQUIDs coupled thereto during the state change to capture instantaneous qubit states while experiencing observable quantum dynamics; and, reading out the instantaneous states. The detector rf-SQUIDs can be a subset of qubits or quantum flux parametrons, leveraging existing on-chip devices. Instantaneous states can be captured across a range of effective measurement bases through iterative modulation of polar and azimuthal angles by sweeping rf-SQUID body biases and annealing delay times.

sources.title: EFFICIENT RESOURCE ALLOCATION FOR ITERATIVE COMBINATORIAL OPTIMIZATION [EP4800550A1]
sources.abstract:
[0001]    A resource allocation method for iteratively improving a solution to a problem by combinatorial optimization including those not natively suited for quantum computers is proposed. Classical and quantum computing resources are provided. Starting from a solution in the search space following steps are repeated:
- deciding whether to use classical or quantum optimization
- in the case of classical optimization, calculating at least one classical estimator with a classical optimization algorithm on provided classical computing resources,
- in the case of quantum optimization, calculating at least one correlation matrix with a quantum optimization algorithm on provided quantum computing resources, and
- updating the solution based on at least one estimator or at least one correlation matrix. The method terminates when a termination criterium is met. The invention provides a flexible optimization problem solving approach for technical systems that can deal with a high level of complexity and overcomes the limitations of existing quantum optimization strategies, thereby offering promising avenues for tackling larger-scale and more complex optimization problems including those not natively suited for quantum computers.

sources.title: Optimizing database join operations using quantum annealing, swarm intelligence, and genetic algorithms [US12717787B1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Systems and methods are disclosed for optimizing database join operations in large-scale relational databases using an integrated framework of quantum annealing, swarm intelligence, and genetic algorithms. The system employs quantum annealing to learn data distribution patterns, normalizing and transforming data to identify optimal join strategies and correlations across tables. Swarm intelligence predicts access patterns by deploying artificial ants to navigate data blocks, converging on high-relevance areas for prefetching. Genetic algorithms estimate join selectivity, calculating expected record counts to allocate resources efficiently. Learned index structures, dynamically created and tuned based on identified patterns, enhance retrieval speed with minimal storage. Additional features include learned Bloom filters for accurate join candidate selection, predictive page loading to reduce I/O wait times, and join order optimization to minimize intermediate result sizes. This modular, adaptive approach ensures rapid, resource-efficient query responses across diverse applications, such as banking and e-commerce.

sources.title: Neural network operator design method, device and equipment for aircraft flow field modeling and medium [CN122635437A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a neural network operator design method and device for aircraft flow field modeling, equipment and a medium, and relates to the field of operator design, and the method comprises the steps: extracting a to-be-replaced linear operator from a target calculation model suitable for an aircraft flow field modeling scene, and obtaining a to-be-replaced linear operator based on an obtained to-be-replaced operator list and operator constraint information; constructing a black box type operator network structure by using a tensor primitive library; iteratively optimizing black box operator generation parameters by using the obtained operator generation result and a quantum annealing algorithm to obtain candidate black box operators; evaluating the candidate black box operator by using a preset precision evaluation index and a preset performance evaluation index, and determining a target deep neural network operator suitable for the aircraft flow field modeling scene; and updating the target solution model by using the target deep neural network operator so as to execute an aircraft flow field modeling operation based on the updated target solution model. According to the method, the operator which is controllable in precision and meets design rules and requirements can be automatically generated, and the flow field modeling effect of the aircraft is improved.

sources.title: Quantum annealing image processing method and system based on path integral Monte Carlo [CN122616668A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a quantum annealing image processing method and system based on path integral Monte Carlo, and relates to the technical field of artificial intelligence, and the method comprises the steps: obtaining demand information for processing a target image; performing quantum bit coding on the basic unit blocks of the neural network model to generate quantum bits; constructing an energy function based on the demand information and the quantum bits; mapping the energy function into a Hamiltonian of quantum annealing; based on the Hamiltonian and the quantum bits, quantum annealing simulation is carried out according to path integral Monte Carlo, and target values of spin state vectors of the quantum bits are obtained; mapping the target value into an image processing model architecture; and processing the target image based on the image processing model architecture to generate an image processing result. According to the method, the basic unit blocks are searched for crossing the energy barrier by utilizing quantum tunneling of quantum annealing, and the architecture search stability and convergence efficiency are improved by virtue of a path integral Monte Carlo method, so that the image can be stably and efficiently processed.

sources.title: Intelligent classified and screened short message directional sending method and system [CN122621871A]
authors: JIANGSU HUILIAN ZHITONG COMMUNICATION TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: JIANGSU HUILIAN ZHITONG COMMUNICATION TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses an intelligent classified and screened short message directional sending method and system, and relates to the field of short message communication. The method comprises the steps of collecting spatio-temporal data of a target user and extracting spatio-temporal features to construct a spatio-temporal portrait of the target user, wherein the spatio-temporal portrait comprises a type preference tag and a scene sensitivity tag; performing multi-objective optimization according to the type preference label and the scene sensitivity label by using a quantum annealing algorithm to obtain sensitivity scores of the target user on different short message types; obtaining a to-be-sent short message, performing quantum feature extraction to obtain quantum bit state features, and performing classification by using a quantum neural network to obtain type tags; and then, according to the type label and the sensitivity score, calculating the sending priority of the short message, and selecting a sending channel to send the short message to the target user in combination with the current network load state. Therefore, short message priority classification pushing can be carried out according to user preferences in a dynamic scene, and the problems of insufficient dynamism, multi-target stiffness and the like of user portrait and short message classification are solved.

sources.title: Thermocouple layout optimization method for pure hydrogen shaft furnace wall heat distribution monitoring [CN122616272A]
authors: AUTOMATION RESEARCH AND DESIGN INST OF METALLURGICAL INDUSTRY CO LTD
BEIJING IRON & STEEL RESEARCH INST HYDROGEN METALLURGY TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH INST CO LTD
sources.organization: AUTOMATION RESEARCH AND DESIGN INST OF METALLURGICAL INDUSTRY CO LTD, BEIJING IRON & STEEL RESEARCH INST HYDROGEN METALLURGY TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH INST CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of industrial process modeling and optimization, and relates to a thermocouple layout optimization method for pure hydrogen shaft furnace wall heat distribution monitoring, which comprises the following steps: constructing a pure hydrogen shaft furnace high-fidelity digital twin model, and generating a full-node temperature field matrix; performing space-time decoupling on the full-node temperature field matrix based on a K-L decomposition method, and extracting a space basis function matrix and a corresponding time coefficient matrix; establishing a thermocouple layout optimization mathematical model based on the full-node temperature field matrix, the binary decision vector, the space basis function matrix and the time coefficient matrix; based on the thermocouple layout optimization mathematical model, an Isin energy function is obtained, a mixed quantum optimization algorithm is adopted for solving, and an optimal thermocouple layout scheme is output. According to the method, efficient solving of the engineering scale sensor layout problem is achieved, the solving quality and the convergence speed are remarkably improved, and a scientific and quantitative layout design scheme is provided for a pure hydrogen shaft furnace temperature monitoring system.

sources.title: Intelligent advertisement putting recommendation system based on big data analysis [CN122573533A]
authors: SUZHOU LINGXI INTERACTIVE ADVERTISING CO LTD
sources.organization: SUZHOU LINGXI INTERACTIVE ADVERTISING CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of advertisement putting frequency control, in particular to an intelligent advertisement putting recommendation system based on big data analysis, which comprises a single data acquisition unit, a data storage processing unit, a putting frequency control unit and an advertisement matching recommendation unit. The data storage processing unit processes data by using an emotional knowledge graph enhanced multi-modal fusion learning method and the like, and the putting frequency control unit sets a recommended frequency threshold value by integrating multiple factors, calculates indexes by using a memory attenuation model inspired by quantum, and obtains a recommended frequency threshold value by means of a self-adaptive monitoring mechanism inspired by biology and a quantum annealing optimization algorithm. Intelligent monitoring and pushing priority adjustment are achieved, the advertisement matching recommendation unit screens advertisements through a holographic matching retrieval algorithm, and through a reinforcement learning algorithm inspired by a brain-computer interface, recommendation strategies are optimized according to real-time feedback of a user, the advertisement putting accuracy and efficiency are improved, the user experience is improved, and the advertisement resource utilization rate is increased.

sources.title: Traditional Chinese and western medicine cooperative senescence prediction and intervention method based on automatic mining of medical record knowledge [CN122552134A]
authors: LIAONING VOCATIONAL COLLEGE OF MEDICINE SCIENCE PARK CO LTD
sources.organization: LIAONING VOCATIONAL COLLEGE OF MEDICINE SCIENCE PARK CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a traditional Chinese and western medicine cooperative senescence prediction and intervention method based on automatic mining of medical record knowledge, and relates to the technical field of senescence assessment, and the method comprises the steps: collecting multi-source heterogeneous data of traditional Chinese medicine constitution, tongue condition, pulse condition, western medicine imaging, blood biochemistry, gene detection and the like, and building an organ unified data model after generative adversarial network expansion; an adaptive data mapping strategy is generated through DQN, data fusion is completed by adopting RF-BiLSTM-Attention, and feature extraction and dimension reduction are realized in combination with APSO-ResNet-Lite and DAE-PCA; based on a two-stage series model formed by IPCO-DBN and a quantum optimization deep neural decision tree, accurate quantification of organ aging risks is completed, an intervention scheme of Chinese and western collaborative adjustment is generated, and closed-loop iterative optimization is assisted. According to the method, deep fusion of traditional Chinese and western medicine data and organ specific aging evaluation are realized, and the accuracy and practicability of aging prediction and intervention are improved.

authors: CHINA MOBILE FINANCE TECH CO LTD
CHINA MOBILE COMMUNICATIONS GROUP CO LTD
